symptom: A command run without `-p` (e.g. `mxcli describe module M`) silently works against a stray `.mpr` in the working directory; the only sign is `Using project: App.mpr`, which reads the same for the intended project and a stray copy. With several `.mpr` files nothing is picked and the command just says `--project (-p) is required`
cause: `rootCmd.PersistentPreRun` auto-discovery (`discoverProjectPath`) printed only the bare file name it set `-p` to, and returned nothing at all when the directory was ambiguous
insight: Auto-detecting the sole `.mpr` is the CLI's documented resolution (init, new, theme and the LSP all do it), so refusing a single match would break `cd app && mxcli ...`; the defect was that the guess was indistinguishable from an explicit choice. Name the absolute path, say it was auto-detected and how to override, and list the candidates when ambiguous. The `-p` value stays the bare file name so nothing downstream sees a different path. Unit-test the helper on a temp dir (no chdir); control: a body returning the old bare notice fails all three content assertions
